videos.title: The One Number That Explains Why Your TIPS Fund Lost to Inflation
videos.summary: Rob Berger answers a viewer whose short-term TIPS ETF returned about 1.7% in a year when inflation ran 3.7%. He explains how a fund's average maturity and duration let rising real yields eat into the inflation adjustment, then compares two ultra-short TIPS funds that kept pace and asks when individual TIPS make more sense than a fund.
videos.why: A clear, short explanation of why owning TIPS through a fund is not the same as being protected from inflation, with the trade-offs laid out.

videos.title: Roth Conversions Won't Save Your Retirement
videos.summary: Using a viewer's case of a 58-year-old couple with large pretax and taxable balances, Berger models Roth conversions that fill the 22% and the 24% brackets and compares them with no conversions. He frames the goal as lower lifetime taxes rather than just avoiding required minimum distributions, and finds the plan's chance of success barely moves either way.
videos.why: A useful corrective to the idea that conversions are always worth it: they can trim lifetime taxes, but they rarely make or break a plan, and he argues against locking in a fixed conversion schedule.

videos.title: The Forever Paycheck: Is Jean Chatzky Right About Annuities?
videos.summary: Rob Berger weighs the case for income annuities, prompted by Jean Chatzky's argument for them, and explains why he is holding off on buying one for now.
videos.why: A practical look at the annuity question from someone who builds his own retirement income, useful for anyone weighing an annuity against other ways to set an income floor.

videos.title: You Could Have Used a 7% Withdrawal Rate
videos.summary: Financial planner Erin Moriarity pushes back on the 4% rule, setting out to show that many past retirees could have spent considerably more than it allows.
videos.why: A counterweight to conservative starting withdrawal rates, worth watching alongside the usual 4% rule discussion.

videos.title: Retirement Guardrails: When to Cut Spending (and When to Spend More)
videos.summary: Rob Berger sets out to explain guardrails withdrawal rules: when a market decline should trigger a cut in retirement spending, and when strong returns allow spending to rise.
videos.why: Guardrails are a common answer to spending more early in retirement without running out later, so this is a practical companion to any debate about withdrawal rates.

videos.title: Anthropic Opened Its Books. What Is It Really Worth?
videos.summary: Former hedge fund manager and finance professor Patrick Boyle sets out to value Anthropic now that its IPO filing has made its financials public, and to weigh that against the price the market is talking about.
videos.why: Boyle is a reliably skeptical voice on hype valuations, and this is one of the most watched takes on a filing that moved AI stocks.

videos.title: Half the S&P Is One AI Trade. This Isn't 1999. What If the Bubble Is in the Safe Stocks?
videos.summary: An Excess Returns conversation, separate from the John Davi episode, that sets out to compare today's AI-heavy market with 1999 and to ask whether the real overvaluation sits in the defensive stocks investors are hiding in.
videos.why: It flips the usual concentration worry, which is worth hearing for anyone shifting toward low-volatility or value stocks as a hedge.

videos.title: Do Democrat Election Victories Mean Future Tax Hikes for Retirees?
videos.summary: Tax planner Sean Mullaney responds to this week's midterm results and sets out to answer whether they make tax increases on retirees more likely. In an earlier post on the same question he argued they remain unlikely, pointing to the growing share of older voters and to the absence of a major tax hike aimed at retirees in more than three decades.
videos.why: Five minutes that test the common argument for doing Roth conversions now before tax rates rise.

videos.title: Bogleheads® Chapter Series – Navigating TIPS (Treasury Inflation -Protected Securities) with Kevin M
videos.summary: A two hour Bogleheads chapter session on Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, presented by Kevin M.
videos.why: A long reference session for anyone using TIPS for inflation-protected retirement income; the slides make it better watched than listened to, and it is easy to skim for the parts that matter.

videos.title: $43K Roth Conversion Tax Free?
videos.summary: Tax planner Sean Mullaney takes up the question in the title: whether a Roth conversion of about $43,000 can be done without owing federal income tax.
videos.why: Mullaney is one of the clearest voices on early-retirement tax planning, and low-income years before Social Security and required distributions are when conversions like this are worth running the numbers on.

videos.title: Should You Stop Saving for Retirement Because of AI? (FQF)
videos.summary: Rob Berger takes on the argument, popular among some tech leaders, that AI-driven abundance will make saving for retirement unnecessary.
videos.why: A widely watched response to a claim that is spreading quickly, and a useful sanity check before anyone changes a savings plan because of it.

videos.title: The Smartest Ways to Withdraw Money in Retirement
videos.summary: PensionCraft backtests the inflation-adjusted 4% rule against guardrail withdrawal rules on US and UK history, and shows that the rules which never run out of money get there by cutting income, in one stagflation-era case by more than half.
videos.why: It frames the decision around two numbers, the income needed and the lowest income that would be acceptable, gives cash buffers a reality check, and closes with the bond ladder plan the presenter would use, which makes it a good stress test for any withdrawal plan.
